title: Fever temperatures modulate intraprotein dynamics and enhance the binding affinity between monoclonal antibodies and the Spike protein from SARS-CoV-2
authors: Dong Gun Kim; Hak Sung Kim; Yoonjoo Choi; Razvan C. Stan
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子动力学模拟研究发热温度对抗体与SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白结合亲和力的影响，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA，且方法为MD可借鉴，但对象与课题核心不符。
abstract: Fever is a typical symptom of most infectious diseases. While prolonged fever may be clinically undesirable, mild reversible fever (< 39°C, 312K) can potentiate the immune responses against pathogens. Here, using molecular dynamics, we investigated the effect of febrile temperatures (38°C to 40°C, 311K to 313K) on the immune complexes formed by the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein with two neutralizing antibodies. We found that, at mild fever temperatures (311-312K), the binding affinities of the two antibodies improve when compared to the physiological body temperature (37°C, 310K). Furthermore, only at 312K, antibodies exert distinct mechanical effects on the receptor binding domains of the spike protein that may hinder SARS-CoV-2 infectivity. Enhanced antibody binding affinity may thus be obtained using appropriate temperature conditions.
abstract_zh: 发热是大多数感染性疾病的典型症状。虽然长期发热在临床上可能不受欢迎，但轻度可逆性发热（< 39°C, 312K）能增强针对病原体的免疫反应。在此，我们利用分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 研究了发热温度（38°C 至 40°C, 311K 至 313K）对SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白与两种中和抗体形成的免疫复合物的影响。我们发现，在轻度发热温度（311-312K）下，与生理体温（37°C, 310K）相比，两种抗体的结合亲和力有所提高。此外，仅在312K时，抗体对刺突蛋白受体结合域产生独特的机械效应，这可能阻碍SARS-CoV-2的感染性。因此，通过适当的温度条件，可以获得增强的抗体结合亲和力。
